data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject rather than describing it exactly when the test is installed into a fail-first adjudication loop before the subject's guard can observe the mutation: the 'shown-to-fail-first' installation reverses the temporal authority of guard and test, so mutations that are visible only to the test's own failure channel are registered as caught even when no guard fired. This is a masking-by-installation-order effect, not a property of the subject.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If every guard had been run to completion before the first test-failure signal was committed, the 3-of-26 result would collapse toward a description of the guards, not the tests.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If at least one surviving mutation's guard had failed on a change visible only in the subject's declared data, the 'added behaviour' costume claim would fail.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the same 3 survivors disappeared under a reordering where tests run after all guards, the installation-order explanation would be refuted.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In the 3-of-26 result, the surviving mutations share a common cost: their guard checks declared data while the mutation adds behaviour. When a mutation is shown-to-fail first, the failing test is registered before the ordinarily-guarded module's guard is evaluated for that mutation, so the guard's failure to see the added behaviour is never counted. The 1/9 compile.py loss and the 4/4 to 6/7 per-module banding follow the same mechanism: modules whose guards fire on the failure-channel-adjacent surface are overcounted, while modules whose guards inspect a structurally disjoint surface (declared vs. added) are undercounted.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
